prompt:
These are my taste in quotes, based from this quotes, give me 30 more real quotes by philospohers: ""To live is to suffer, to survive is to find some meaning in the suffering."
- Friedrich Nietzsche

"The journey of a thousand miles begins with one step."
- Loa Tzu

"The only way to deal with an unfree world is to become so absolutely free that your very existence is an act of rebellion."
- Albert Camus

"It is not wisdom but Authority that makes a law."
- Thomas Hobbes

“The most difficult thing in life is to know yourself.”
- Thales

“Give a man a fish and you feed him for a day; teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime.”
-	Maimonides"
answer:
1. “We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.” — Seneca, *Letters to Lucilius* 13

2. “It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste much of it.” — Seneca, *On the Shortness of Life*

3. “Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views they take of them.” — Epictetus, *Enchiridion* 5

4. “No man is free who is not master of himself.” — Epictetus, *Discourses*

5. “The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.” — Marcus Aurelius, *Meditations* 5.20

6. “Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.” — Marcus Aurelius, *Meditations* 10.16

7. “The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts.” — Marcus Aurelius, *Meditations* 5.16

8. “He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.” — Friedrich Nietzsche, *Twilight of the Idols*

9. “That which does not kill us makes us stronger.” — Friedrich Nietzsche, *Twilight of the Idols*

10. “No one can build you the bridge on which you, and only you, must cross the river of life.” — Friedrich Nietzsche, *Schopenhauer as Educator*

11. “Man is condemned to be free.” — Jean-Paul Sartre, *Existentialism Is a Humanism*

12. “Existence precedes essence.” — Jean-Paul Sartre, *Existentialism Is a Humanism*

13. “Hell is other people.” — Jean-Paul Sartre, *No Exit*

14. “The absurd is born of this confrontation between the human need and the unreasonable silence of the world.” — Albert Camus, *The Myth of Sisyphus*

15. “One must imagine Sisyphus happy.” — Albert Camus, *The Myth of Sisyphus*

16. “In the depth of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer.” — Albert Camus, “Return to Tipasa”

17. “I rebel—therefore we exist.” — Albert Camus, *The Rebel*

18. “Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.” — Søren Kierkegaard, *Journals*

19. “Anxiety is the dizziness of freedom.” — Søren Kierkegaard, *The Concept of Anxiety*

20. “The unexamined life is not worth living.” — Socrates, in Plato’s *Apology*

21. “Wonder is the beginning of philosophy.” — Plato, *Theaetetus*

22. “Man is by nature a political animal.” — Aristotle, *Politics*

23. “The greatest thing in the world is to know how to belong to oneself.” — Michel de Montaigne, *Essays*

24. “Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.” — Jean-Jacques Rousseau, *The Social Contract*

25. “I think, therefore I am.” — René Descartes, *Discourse on Method*

26. “The heart has its reasons, which reason does not know.” — Blaise Pascal, *Pensées*

27. “Man is a thinking reed.” — Blaise Pascal, *Pensées*

28. “A man can do what he wills, but he cannot will what he wills.” — Arthur Schopenhauer, *On the Freedom of the Will*

29. “Sapere aude! Have courage to use your own understanding.” — Immanuel Kant, *What Is Enlightenment?*

30. “Better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied.” — John Stuart Mill, *Utilitarianism*
